standard_prerequisites.name: Church numerals as iterators
standard_prerequisites.statement: The Church numeral of m applied to f and x applies f to x exactly m times.
standard_prerequisites.use: It underwrites both halves of the iteration count in the proof (490-501).

standard_prerequisites.name: Lambda definability
standard_prerequisites.statement: A number-theoretic function f is lambda definable when some term applied to the Church numerals of the arguments reduces to the Church numeral of the value.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the criterion the displayed Mult term must meet (482-501).

core_obligations: Beta-reduce Mult applied to the numerals n and m to the abstraction applying n to (m f) and x (490-495).
The numeral m applied to f is the function iterating f m times; iterating that function n times over x applies f to x n times m times (495-499).
The normal form is the Church numeral of n times m, so Mult lambda defines multiplication (499-501).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce the application to the iterated form.
Count the iterations and identify the normal form.

difficulty_reason: The counted proposition is the author proposition at source lines 482-488: multiplication is lambda definable by the term Mult equalling the abstraction that applies a to (b f) and then to x. The author proof (490-501) is a complete reduction walk: applying Mult to Church numerals n and m reduces to an abstraction applying the numeral n to (m-numeral applied to f) and x; since the numeral m applied to f iterates f m times, the composed iteration applies f to x exactly n times m times, i.e., n times m times; and the resulting normal form is exactly the Church numeral of the product. The reduction chain and the iteration count are both carried in the proof; the later editorial note on eta-reduction and the exercise on an alternative term are outside the counted proof.
